**Step 1 — Scene:** A small breakfast-style meal with bacon, roasted potatoes, strawberries, and what appears to be pineapple.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A square plate, approximately 21–22 cm across its sides. Using an equivalent circular diameter of about 24 cm gives an area of **3.14 × 12² = 452 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Strawberry pieces, two pineapple pieces, cooked bacon, and skin-on roasted potato chunks. No separate sauce is visible; cooking fat is included in the potatoes’ energy estimate.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate coverage | Area | Height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Strawberries | 13% | 59 cm² | 1.6 cm | 94 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 56 g | 32 | 18 kcal |
| Pineapple | 10% | 45 cm² | 1.6 cm | 72 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 47 g | 50 | 24 kcal |
| Bacon | 9% | 41 cm² | 0.5 cm | 21 ml | 0.90 g/ml | 19 g | 500 | 95 kcal |
| Roasted potatoes | 23% | 104 cm² | 1.9 cm | 198 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 129 g | 160 | 206 kcal |

Coverage totals **55%**, consistent with the substantial exposed plate. Volumes are area × height; weights apply the bulk-density reduction only.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **251 g and 343 kcal** is plausible for this modest plate. The bacon is a small portion despite its curled footprint, and the potatoes provide most of the weight and energy. Potato oil content and the identification of the yellow fruit are the main uncertainties.
